figs.name: scada-communication-problems-troubleshooting-flowchart
figs.alt: SCADA communication problems troubleshooting flowchart checking network, then PLC, then SCADA
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing the field rule for SCADA faults: ping and check the network first, compare raw PLC values second, then check client and SCADA settings last.
figs.after_h2: Most Common Root Causes of SCADA Communication Problems (From Field Experience)

figs.name: scada-communication-problems-wrong-value-check-infographic
figs.alt: SCADA showing 35 bar while PLC shows 50 bar with scaling and address checks
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing the wrong value case where the PLC reads 50 bar but SCADA shows 35 bar, and the mapping, scaling and raw value checks that find it.
figs.after_h2: 3. SCADA Shows Wrong Values (But PLC Is Correct)

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 500" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">

<rect width="800" height="500" fill="#ffffff"/>

<text x="190" y="108" font-size="18" fill="#e5e7eb" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">PLC value</text>
<text x="190" y="162" font-size="36" fill="#16a34a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">50 bar</text>
<rect x="480" y="70" width="260" height="120" rx="14" fill="#111827" stroke="#be123c" stroke-width="4"/>

<rect x="60" y="408" width="680" height="68" rx="10" fill="#fff1f2" stroke="#be123c" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="95" cy="442" r="17" fill="#be123c"/>
